answer.text: alert to its appeal but unconvinced by it
answer.line: Paragraph 16 grants the image its appeal, then says the language of intention has run well ahead of the measurements.

steps: Find where the author names the image: paragraph 16, the web of nurture.
Collect both halves of the verdict. Warm: "the appeal is easy to see", and some of it is defensible as metaphor. Cool: the claims ran ahead of the measurements.
Keep both halves. Appeal granted, belief withheld.

choices.text: alert to its appeal but unconvinced by it
choices.note: Appeal granted in sentence 2, belief withheld in sentence 4: both halves, at the author's strength.

choices.text: indifferent to whether the image is accurate
choices.note: The author cares about accuracy: sentence 4 sets the claims against the measurements and the sources cited for them.

choices.text: fully persuaded by the case that has been made for it
choices.note: Paragraph 16 says the opposite: the confident language has run well ahead of the measurements.

choices.text: openly contemptuous of everyone who repeats it
choices.note: The author grants the appeal and calls some of it defensible as metaphor. That is measured doubt about claims, not scorn for people.

choices.text: amused that researchers have allowed the phrase to spread so widely
choices.note: Nothing in paragraph 16 is played for laughs. The author treats the overreach as a real problem with the claims.

lockIt: Tone: when the author grants one thing and doubts another, the answer keeps both halves.
